clue.text: I don't dance with everyone following description of depression?

parts.note: everyone means all
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lower describes the act of depressing something, pushing it down

explanation.surface: Someone at a party explains why they sit out every dance: they are feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a first-person line spoken by a shy person who sits at the edge of the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is the shy guest left standing by the wall at a dance, without a partner.

clue.text: Henry not appearing full-frontal in part of London

seen end-on, an object is facing you edge first rather than with its full face

explanation.surface: A man called Henry keeps his clothes on somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hendon is a suburb in north London. END-ON describes something seen from its end, not its broad front.
explanation.definitionFit: Hendon is a district in the London Borough of Barnet, in the north of the city.

clue.text: Politician's attitude in support of one's damages

airs are an affected manner or attitude

explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the politician's airs sit beneath ('in support of') the I for one, so I comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, a synonym of damage as a verb.

clue.text: Nervous article, testy in odd places

clue.text: But can't I keep the lens? Nonsense!

definitions.text: But can't I keep the lens?
definitions.meaning: a protest from someone losing part of the eye, who wants to keep all of it

explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical first half: the lens is part of the eye, so someone who wants to keep it wants the whole of their eye.
explanation.definitionFit: All my eye is an old British idiom for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: I can't wait for some bread before working

explanation.definitionFit: Literature is the body of written imaginative work, novels, plays and verse.
